extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary) and patent practitioners/applicants (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures for examination of U.S. patent applications (MPEP Chapter 700): what examiners may require, how searches should be performed, how informalities and replies are handled, and rules for expunging submitted information. Focused on complying with 35 U.S.C. and 37 C.F.R. provisions (e.g., 37 CFR 1.105, 1.56, 1.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for examination and main patentability conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority for examination derives from 35 U.S.C. 131 (Director shall cause an examination), and the main conditions precedent to the grant of a patent are set forth in 35 U.S.C. 101, 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 101 defines patentable subject matter (new and useful process, machine, manufacture, composition of matter, or improvement). Use form paragraph 7.04 which copies 35 U.S.C. 101. Examiners must determine entitlement to a patent under these statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites of the application (35 U.S.C. 111(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new application is assigned to a Technology Center, the examiner should review contents to determine if the application meets requirements of 35 U.S.C. 111(a), including matters affecting filing date or abandonment (oath/declaration, filing fee, claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check formal matters and completeness/clarity of disclosure per MPEP Chapter 600 before placing application in storage. If requisites not met, applicant may be called upon for necessary amendments; such amendments must not include new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of obviously informal or insufficient disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If impractical to give a complete action on the merits due to informal/insufficient disclosure, follow specific procedure: reasonable search as far as disclosure permits; point out informalities; require specification be revised to idiomatic English/US practice; reject claims that fail to define invention under 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosure incomprehensible so as to preclude reasonable search, state no search made. Use attachments to point out informalities (see MPEP §707.07(a)). Blanket rejection of informal claims usually sufficient. Treat multiple obviously informal claims as a single claim for fee/examination purposes. Applicants are urged to submit preliminary amendment (preferably within 3 months) correcting obvious informalities; such preliminary amendments must exclude new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of terminology / when the disclosure is incomprehensible
rubrics_metrics.description: If terminology is so different from art-accepted terminology that a proper search cannot be made, require applicant to clarify or correlate terminology so a proper comparison with prior art can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.01 when terminology prevents examination; use form paragraph 7.02 where disclosure is incomprehensible and precludes reasonable search. Set a shortened statutory period for reply (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer). Indicate problematic pages/terms in brackets of form paragraphs. Advise applicant not to introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search obligations and treatment of previous examiner's search
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading the specification and claims, examiner searches the prior art; the invention should be thoroughly understood before searching. When assigned after previous actions, give full faith and credit to previous examiner's search/action unless clear error or knowledge of other prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reorient case or take entirely new approach merely to hope of finding something. See MPEP §904–904.03 for searching practice. Informal or imperfectly understood cases still receive a search to avoid piecemeal prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to require information (37 CFR 1.105) — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: In examining or treating a matter in a pending or abandoned application (or patent, reexamination), the examiner may require submission from individuals identified under 37 CFR 1.56(c) or an assignee such information as may be reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.105 permits requiring e.g., commercial databases known to inventors, whether a prior art search was made and what was searched, copies of non-patent literature/published applications/patents related to the claimed invention or used to draft the application or used in the invention process, identification of improvements, identification of any use of the claimed invention known to inventors at filing, etc. Where assignee asserts right to prosecute, such requirements may apply to assignee. A reply that required information is unknown/not readily available will be accepted as complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for 'information reasonably necessary' (reasonable necessity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 may be made only when the examiner has a reasonable basis for requiring information that would aid examination or treatment; scope should be narrowly defined and focused to minimize burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical need is for finding prior art or resolving issues from search/analysis. Requirement is not a substitute for examiner performing a search per MPEP §704.01 and §§904–904.03. Reasonable necessity is generally met where: (A) claimed subject matter cannot be adequately searched by class/keyword among patents and typical non-patent literature sources; or (B) the application file or lack of relevant prior art found justifies asking applicant if they have relevant information. Provide narrow, specifically focused requests and state the basis for requiring information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of information that may be reasonably required (non-exhaustive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific examples listed in MPEP §704.11(a) of information that may be reasonably required under 37 CFR 1.105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: name/citation of any particularly relevant indexed journal or treatise; trade names of goods/services embodying the claimed subject matter; citations/dates/copies of advertising/promotional literature; citations/copies of journal articles describing goods/services embodying claimed subject matter; trade names/providers of competing goods/services; written descriptions/analyses prepared by inventors/assignees of competitive goods/services; identification of pending/abandoned applications by the inventors or assignee disclosing similar subject matter not identified in current application; reply to a protest under 37 CFR 1.291; explanation of technical material in a publication (e.g., inventor's publication); identification of changes in reformatted continuing applications; mark-up for CIPs showing added subject matter; comments on Federal Circuit decisions on point; publication date of undated document mentioned by applicant; comments raising question of derivation under 35 U.S.C. 102(f). These are illustrative, not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to make a requirement for information (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 is discretionary and may be made at any time once necessity is recognized; optimum time is prior to or with the first action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily do not make such a request with or after a final rejection. It may be appropriate prior to the first action in newly established art areas without well-developed prior art, where applicant submitted an IDS, where the specification's background is inadequate, where related documents by inventor/assignee are found but not submitted, where non-patent literature is referred but copies not supplied, or where background admissions unfamiliar to examiner cannot be found via search. Requirements made after first action are rarely appropriate and should be for matters justifying further action by examiner (i.e., usually non-final actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to a requirement for information — completeness and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies must be complete and filed within the time period set (including extensions). Failure to reply will result in abandonment. Replies stating information is unknown/not readily available will be accepted as complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All replies should be checked for completeness; any incomplete reply can be completed within the original time period (including extensions). Supplemental replies filed after expiration of original period (including extensions) must comply with rules for submissions of information. A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 is an Office action even if no action on the merits is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of 37 CFR 1.105 requirements to the duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of candor under 37 CFR 1.56 applies to replies to 1.105 requirements, but the thresholds differ: 1.56 requires disclosure of information material to patentability (a substantially higher threshold), while 1.105 requires information reasonably necessary to examination/treatment (a lower threshold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 1.105 applicant is required to submit information already known (but not required to search for unknown information). Information required under 1.105 might not be material to patentability but may be necessary to determine state of the art, context, or to proceed with examination. Applicants must reply with information reasonably and readily available, consistent with duty of candor.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a complete reply to a 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply is a reply to each enumerated requirement for information giving either the information required or a statement that the information is unknown and/or not readily available to the party or parties from which it was requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant need not prove the information was not in fact readily attainable, but must make a good faith attempt and reasonable inquiry once the information is requested. A reply stating unknown/not readily available will generally be sufficient unless it is clear applicant did not understand the requirement or the reply is ambiguous and a more specific answer is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of incomplete replies to 1.105 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An incomplete reply in a pending application or reexamination proceeding is handled like an amendment not fully responsive to a non-final office action (37 CFR 1.135(c) and MPEP §714.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the reply is a bona fide reply, form paragraph 7.95 may be used. Note that a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement, even without an action on the merits, is an Office action. Follow procedures for non-responsive amendments for examining and notifying applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to avoid introducing new matter in preliminary or corrective amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary amendments or amendments correcting informalities must not introduce 'new matter' because preliminary amendments do not enjoy original disclosure status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise applicants to exclude new matter from preliminary amendments (see MPEP §608.04(b)). If applicant makes amendments, examiner should ensure they conform to U.S. practice and do not add unsupported subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement of information or copies of papers (37 CFR 1.59) — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in an application will not be expunged and returned except as provided in 37 CFR 1.59(b); information forming part of the original disclosure (specification, claims, drawings, preliminary amendment in oath/declaration) will not be expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) with the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) must be filed to request expungement of information not part of the original disclosure. The petition must establish to Commissioner's satisfaction that return is appropriate. See MPEP §724 for factors and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and required showing for petition to expunge (37 CFR 1.59(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To expunge and return information (not part of original disclosure), petitioner must pay fee and establish that (A) the information contains trade secret/proprietary/protected-order material not made public, or (B) the information was unintentionally submitted and failure to return it would cause irreparable harm, and the information has not otherwise been made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision on such petitions is usually held in abeyance until the application is allowed, an Ex parte Quayle action mailed, or application abandoned; at that time a Technology Center Director decides. If information was submitted under MPEP §724.02 (trade secret/proprietary/protective order) there are specific factors (MPEP §724.05) to satisfy to obtain return without petition. Returned information generally must be retained by petitioner for the life of any patent issuing on the application, and expungement is not granted where information is deemed material to patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling information submitted in incorrect application
rubrics_metrics.description: When papers were unintentionally placed in the wrong application file (e.g., wrong heading), a petition should request return; if the Office can determine correct intended application from identifying information, the Office will transfer the papers to the correct file without petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) where appropriate. If transfer is possible based on application number, filing date, title, inventor name, etc., examiner/Office will transfer instead of returning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information forming part of original disclosure cannot be expunged without waiver (37 CFR 1.183)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to expunge parts of the original disclosure must be filed under 37 CFR 1.183 because expunging original disclosure requires waiver of 37 CFR 1.59(a) requirements; such petitions should explain why justice requires waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions to expunge original disclosure are ordinarily not favorably entertained because original disclosures are scanned and part of the official record; granting would require altering USPTO record of originally filed application, which may not be possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and form paragraphs for decisions on petitions to expunge
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP provides form paragraphs to hold petitions in abeyance (7.204), to grant (7.205) or to dismiss (7.206–7.213) petitions to expunge, with specific concluding paragraphs addressing various deficiencies (e.g., lack of fee, information material to patentability, information made public, no commitment to retain, unclear statements/identification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition granted, expunged material returned and petitioner must retain expunged materials for life of any patent issued. If petition dismissed, provide specific explanation citing why information is material/public/lacked commitment/unclear identification/etc. Technology Center Director generally decides petitions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' obligation to narrowly define and focus information requests to minimize applicant burden
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 places a substantial burden on the applicant that is to be minimized by clearly focusing the reason for the requirement and the scope of the expected response; the scope should be narrowly defined and a reasonable basis provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid broad, unfocused requests. State the specific reason information is needed and limit requests to what is reasonably necessary to aid examination (e.g., particular journal names, specific documents, specific aspects of search).
